opening_message:
Ticket 1: Nathaniel Young (employee ID E031) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E031.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Nathaniel Young (E031) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. As the role owns the Payroll system, the maximum access level is admin. Requested write access is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E031 as a contractor with basic security training (note: HR listed full-time). As a contractor with basic training, the maximum allowed access is read. Requested write exceeds this maximum, so recommend read.
reason: There is conflicting information about E031's employment type: HR lists full-time Payroll Specialist (recommending write), while the Security database lists contractor with basic security training (recommending read). If E031 is a contractor with basic training, policy caps access at read, and the requested write exceeds that maximum. Given the unresolved conflict, I apply the more restrictive interpretation, granting read — the maximum permitted level under the contractor/basic-training classification and no more than requested.
